name: ansible-flow-designer
description: Visual, top-down designer for Ansible automation flows: sketch typed nodes and ports, run a walking skeleton, then bind nodes to modules, roles and playbooks.

afd.codegen.onSave.markdownDescription: Write generated code to `generated/` next to the flow whenever a flow without errors is saved. Files edited by hand are never overwritten without asking.

afd.environment.kind.markdownDescription: Where Ansible runs. `auto`: a container when an image is set (here or in the Red Hat Ansible extension's execution environment settings), else a local interpreter (VS Code Remote, venv). Native Windows needs a container.

afd.environment.image.markdownDescription: Execution environment image for the probe and runs, e.g. `registry.example.net/ee/netops:2.19`. Empty: use `ansible.executionEnvironment.image` when the Red Hat Ansible extension enables execution environments.

afd.environment.containerEngine.description: Container engine for the image (auto: the Red Hat Ansible setting, else docker).

afd.environment.containerOptions.markdownDescription: Extra `docker run` / `podman run` arguments, one per item (e.g. `-v`, `~/.ssh:/home/ansible/.ssh:ro` for keys).

afd.environment.python.markdownDescription: Python with ansible-core 2.19+ for local mode. Empty: `ansible.python.interpreterPath`, else `python3`.

afd.run.inventory.markdownDescription: Inventory for runs, relative to the repository root. Empty: the default from `ansible.cfg`.

afd.run.askVaultPassword.markdownDescription: Ask for the vault password before a run (`auto`: when the inventory or repository vars contain vault data). The password is used for that run only and never stored.

afd.awx.url.markdownDescription: AWX address for _Launch in AWX_, e.g. `https://awx.example.net`. The token is kept in VS Code's secret storage (_Set AWX Token_), never in settings.

afd.awx.verifyTls.markdownDescription: Verify AWX's TLS certificate. Turn off only for a lab AWX with a self-signed certificate.

anyOf.description: Add a node. after continues from an output port: a free port is wired to the new node, a wired one gets the node on its wire (so a chain grows: a new flow is start -> done). on_wire does the same for a wired port only, failed_to wires its failed_hosts. The key comes from the title unless given. Use in to add it inside a subflow.

type.description: start (one, on the top level; hosts enter), end (hosts leave; outcome success or failed), task, subflow (has an inner level), decision (true/false per host), approval (a person approves), parallel (branches), join (branches meet).

title.description: Human name shown on the canvas.

key.description: Key of the new node; default: from the title. Must be new on its level.

in.description: Subflow whose inner level gets the node (default: top).

after.description: Continue from this output port: wired to the new node, or the node goes on its wire when the port is wired already.

on_wire.description: Put the new node on the wire leaving this output port (between both ends).

failed_to.description: Wire the new node's failed_hosts to this node.

intent.description: What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.

items.description: A port name. Which ports a node has depends on its type: see the port catalog. Parallel branch ports are branch_1, branch_2, ...

ports.description: Optional ports enabled beyond the type defaults (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task).

handler.description: Marks a failure handler node (what kind of handling it does)

condition.description: Decision nodes: Jinja expression evaluated per host.

branches.description: Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)

join_mode.description: Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one

walkthroughs.title: Design your first Ansible flow
walkthroughs.description: Sketch automation as a diagram of steps wired port to port, handle every failure, and run it as a walking skeleton.

steps.title: Open a sample or start a new flow
steps.description:
A flow is a diagram kept as YAML (`*.flow.yaml`) next to your playbooks. Copy a sample into this folder, or start from scratch with a start and a done node.
[Open Sample Flow](command:afd.openSample)
[New Flow](command:afd.newFlow)
Tip: an empty folder is fine. [Tutorial: your first flow](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F01-first-flow.md%22%5D)

media.altText: A firewall upgrade flow on the designer canvas

steps.title: Add steps
steps.description:
Click or drag a node type from the palette, drag from a port and release on empty canvas, or right-click the canvas for **Add node here…**. To put a step between two nodes, click the wire's port and choose **Insert node on this wire**.
Wires run from an output port (`ok_hosts`, `failed_hosts`, …) to the next node's `in`. Hosts travel along them.
[How-to: canvas basics](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fcanvas-basics.md%22%5D)

media.altText: Quick add inserting a task on a wire

steps.title: Handle every failure
steps.description:
An amber port is a failure nobody handles yet, and the banner counts them. Click it: wire a handler with one click (rollback, notify and stop, exclude and report, retry), or leave it open on purpose with a reason.
[How-to: ports and failure patterns](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fports-and-failure-patterns.md%22%5D)

media.altText: The port menu of an open failed_hosts port

steps.title: Go top-down with subflows
steps.description:
Keep the top level short: a subflow holds the details of one phase. Add a **Subflow** node and double-click it, or select connected steps and choose **Extract into subflow**.
[How-to: subflows](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fsubflows.md%22%5D)

media.altText: The inner level of a pre-checks subflow

steps.title: Check the design
steps.description:
The designer checks the flow as you edit: missing wires, unhandled failures, data a step reads that nothing provides. Problems go to the Problems panel, each with its fix.
[Validate Design](command:afd.validate)
[Reference: problem codes](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22reference%2Fproblems.md%22%5D)

media.altText: The banner counting open fail ports

steps.title: See the generated playbook
steps.description:
Saving a flow without errors writes `generated/<key>.yml` next to it, one play per step. Select a node to see its play in the inspector.
[Generate Playbook](command:afd.generate)
[How-to: code generation](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fcode-generation.md%22%5D)

media.altText: The inspector showing a node and its generated play

steps.title: Run it as a walking skeleton
steps.description:
Steps without code run as TODO messages, so the whole flow runs from the first minute: `ansible-playbook --check` in your Ansible environment (an execution environment image, WSL or a venv). Run mode then shows how many hosts took each wire.
[Run as Skeleton](command:afd.runSkeleton)
[How-to: runs and environments](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fruns-and-environments.md%22%5D)

media.altText: Run mode with host counts on every wire

steps.title: Keep going
steps.description:
Bind steps to modules from your environment's catalog, pass data between them, poll until a device is back, and run for real or in AWX.
[Open the User Guide](command:afd.openGuide)
[Tutorial: from design to production](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F02-design-to-production.md%22%5D)

walkthroughs.title: Build flows with an AI assistant
walkthroughs.description: Copilot, Claude Code, Codex and other agents learn the flow format and edit flows by key with the flow tools.

steps.title: Copilot is ready
steps.description:
In Copilot's agent mode the `ansible-flow` skill and seven flow tools are there without setup. Ask for a flow, or for a change to the open one.
[Open Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)

steps.title: Set up Claude Code, Codex and other agents
steps.description:
Agents in a terminal or another editor need the skill copied and the flow tools registered once. The extension offers it when it finds them; you can also run it any time.
[Set Up AI Assistants](command:afd.setupAi)
[How-to: AI assistants](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fai-assistants.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Ask for a flow
steps.description:
Say what the automation should achieve, how it is split into phases and what happens to failed hosts. The agent builds the flow with all-or-nothing edits and fixes the problems it causes.
[Tutorial: build a flow with an AI assistant](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F04-ai-assistant.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Review and fix
steps.description:
The canvas shows every edit. Check the Problems panel, and ask the agent to fix what is left without changing the logic.
[Validate Design](command:afd.validate)

walkthroughs.title: Run your flows in AWX
walkthroughs.description: Turn a flow into an AWX job template or approval workflow, launch it from VS Code and follow it on the canvas.

steps.title: Connect to AWX
steps.description:
Point the extension at your AWX and store a personal access token in VS Code's secret storage.
[Open the AWX setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22afd.awx.url%22%5D)
[Set AWX Token](command:afd.awx.setToken)

steps.title: Set up the template
steps.description:
Create the job template (or the approval workflow) for the open flow, in the AWX project that holds your repository.
[Set Up AWX Template](command:afd.awx.setupTemplate)
[How-to: AWX](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fawx.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Approvals become AWX approvals
steps.description:
Top-level approval nodes split the flow into a workflow with an approval node at each gate. Local runs approve by themselves, or take the outcome you pass in `afd_approvals`.
[How-to: approvals](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fapprovals.md%22%5D)

steps.title: Launch and follow the run
steps.description:
Launch asks for the flow inputs and confirms the targets and the commit. Run mode shows every node's hosts, failures and times, and offers to mark nodes tested after a passing run.
[Launch in AWX](command:afd.awx.launch)
[Tutorial: AWX end to end](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22tutorials%2F03-awx-end-to-end.md%22%5D)

media.altText: Run mode replaying an AWX job

steps.title: Import an existing AWX workflow
steps.description:
Turn a workflow job template you already have into a flow, laid out top-down, from AWX or from an `awx export` file.
[Import AWX Workflow](command:afd.importAwxWorkflow)
[How-to: import an AWX workflow](command:afd.openGuide?%5B%22how-to%2Fimport-awx.md%22%5D)

media.altText: A flow imported from an AWX workflow
